passage.title: Talent Starts, Perseverance Finishes
paras: We love to believe in natural talent. It is a comforting story: some people are simply born great. But look closely at almost any achievement and you will find years of quiet, unglamorous effort. A pianist's 'gift' is thousands of hours of practice. A scientist's breakthrough follows hundreds of failed experiments. Talent may open the door, but it is perseverance that walks through it, again and again, especially when the room on the other side is hard. The question is not 'Are you gifted?' but 'Will you keep going?'

Think of the footballer who stays behind after training to practise free kicks in the rain, or the pupil who rewrites an essay for the third time. Nobody films those moments. Yet they are where improvement really happens.

Perseverance is not the same as stubbornness. It means keeping the goal and changing the method: asking for help, trying a new approach, resting and returning. Small steps, repeated, add up: a page a day becomes a book; a mile a day becomes a marathon.

So next time you see someone who seems 'naturally' brilliant, ask what you did not see. And next time you find something hard, remember: the struggle is not a sign you should stop. It is usually a sign that you are learning.
